description: Third A1 content batch for The Sound Maze. Challenge uses closer sound contrasts and less obvious spelling patterns while keeping every spoken target distinguishable.

questions.explain: Luck has the /ʌ/ vowel. Lock has /ɑ/, lick has /ɪ/, and look has /ʊ/ in General American pronunciation.
Full has the /ʊ/ vowel. Fool has /u/, fill has /ɪ/, and fell has /ɛ/.
Must has the /ʌ/ vowel. Mist has /ɪ/, mast has /æ/, and most has /oʊ/.
Chair begins with /tʃ/, the sound heard at the start of chair. Share begins with /ʃ/, dare with /d/, and care with /k/.
Jam begins with /dʒ/. Yam begins with /j/, sham with /ʃ/, and ham with /h/.
That begins with the voiced /ð/ sound, written th. Vat begins with /v/, tat with /t/, and sat with /s/.
Much ends with /tʃ/. Mush ends with /ʃ/, must with /t/, and muck with /k/.
Save ends with the voiced /v/ sound. Safe ends with /f/, same with /m/, and sale with /l/.
Badge ends with /dʒ/, written ge. Batch ends with /tʃ/, bad with /d/, and bag with /g/.
Phone begins with ph, which spells the /f/ sound. Tone begins with /t/, bone with /b/, and fine begins with /f/ but has a different vowel and ending.
The k in knock is silent, so the word begins with /n/. Rock, lock, and sock begin with /r/, /l/, and /s/.
The w in wrist is silent, so the word begins with /r/. List begins with /l/, while rest and west begin with /r/ and /w/ but have different vowel or consonant sounds.
